subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A medical student reviewing pancreatic embryology notes that the pancreas forms from two outgrowths of the foregut. She wants to recall which portion is contributed solely by the ventral pancreatic bud.
question: Which of the following pancreatic structures is derived exclusively from the ventral pancreatic bud?

options.text: Tail
Uncinate process
Body
Head
Main pancreatic duct

explanation_correct: The ventral pancreatic bud gives rise to the uncinate process. It also contributes, together with the dorsal bud, to the head and main pancreatic duct. The dorsal bud alone forms the body and tail. This is a classic foregut-derivative fact frequently tested alongside annular pancreas and pancreas divisum.

explanation_incorrect.A: The tail arises from the dorsal pancreatic bud, not the ventral bud.
explanation_incorrect.C: The body of the pancreas is derived from the dorsal bud.
explanation_incorrect.D: The head is formed by both ventral and dorsal buds together, so it is not ventral-only.
explanation_incorrect.E: The main pancreatic duct receives contributions from both buds, so it is not exclusively ventral.

educationalObjective: The ventral pancreatic bud alone forms the uncinate process, whereas both buds form the head and main pancreatic duct.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A newborn presents with forceful vomiting shortly after feeds. Imaging shows a ring of pancreatic tissue encircling the second (descending) portion of the duodenum with narrowing of its lumen. The infant has features of Down syndrome.
question: Which of the following embryologic errors best explains this finding?

options.text: Failure of the dorsal pancreatic bud to develop
Failure of the ventral and dorsal buds to fuse at 7 weeks
Abnormal rotation of the ventral pancreatic bud
Persistence of the fetal umbilical vein within the falciform ligament
Failure of recanalization of the duodenal lumen

explanation_correct: Annular pancreas results from abnormal rotation of the ventral pancreatic bud, which forms a ring of pancreatic tissue around the second part of the duodenum. This can produce duodenal narrowing and vomiting. It is classically associated with Down syndrome. The key distinguishing feature is the encircling ring of pancreatic tissue rather than a simple absence of the lumen.

explanation_incorrect.A: Dorsal bud agenesis would remove the body and tail, not create a ring around the duodenum.
explanation_incorrect.B: Failure of the buds to fuse at 7 weeks produces pancreas divisum, which is usually asymptomatic and does not form a duodenal ring.
explanation_incorrect.D: A patent fetal umbilical vein (ligamentum teres) is a vascular remnant of the falciform ligament and is unrelated to the pancreas.
explanation_incorrect.E: Failure of duodenal recanalization produces duodenal atresia with a double-bubble sign, but no encircling pancreatic ring.

educationalObjective: Annular pancreas is caused by abnormal rotation of the ventral bud and can encircle the second duodenum, especially in Down syndrome.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 34-year-old woman has two episodes of acute epigastric pain with elevated lipase over two years, with no gallstones or alcohol use. MRCP reveals a pancreas in which the ventral and dorsal ductal systems drain separately, with the dorsal duct draining through the minor papilla.
question: Which of the following best describes the embryologic basis of this anatomy?

options.text: Abnormal rotation of the ventral bud around the duodenum
Complete failure of the dorsal bud to form
Hypertrophy of the uncinate process
Failure of the ventral and dorsal pancreatic buds to fuse at 7 weeks
Persistence of the accessory pancreatic duct as the sole drainage pathway

explanation_correct: Pancreas divisum occurs when the ventral and dorsal pancreatic parts fail to fuse at 7 weeks of development. It is a common anomaly and is mostly asymptomatic, but it may cause chronic abdominal pain and/or pancreatitis in some patients. Separate drainage through the minor and major papillae reflects the two unfused ductal systems. This is distinct from annular pancreas, which is a rotational defect.

explanation_incorrect.A: Abnormal ventral bud rotation causes annular pancreas, a ring of tissue around the duodenum, not separate ductal systems.
explanation_incorrect.B: Dorsal bud failure would remove most of the pancreas, including body and tail, which is not the case here.
explanation_incorrect.C: Uncinate hypertrophy is not a recognized embryologic failure and would not split the ductal systems.
explanation_incorrect.E: The accessory duct may persist, but the underlying defect is nonfusion of the two buds, not persistence of a single duct.

educationalObjective: Pancreas divisum results from failed fusion of the ventral and dorsal buds at 7 weeks and is usually asymptomatic but can cause pain or pancreatitis.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: During a dissection, a student notes that the spleen lies within the mesentery of the stomach. She is asked about the spleen's embryonic origin and its arterial supply.
question: Which of the following statements about the spleen is correct?

options.text: It arises from endoderm of the foregut and is supplied by the superior mesenteric artery
It arises from endoderm of the midgut and is supplied by the splenic branch of the celiac trunk
It arises from mesoderm of the dorsal mesogastrium but is supplied by the superior mesenteric artery
It arises from ectoderm near the diaphragm and is supplied by the inferior phrenic artery
It arises from mesoderm of the dorsal mesogastrium but has a foregut blood supply via the celiac trunk and splenic artery

explanation_correct: The spleen arises in the mesentery of the stomach (dorsal mesogastrium) and is therefore mesodermal. However, it receives a foregut blood supply: the celiac trunk gives rise to the splenic artery. This dissociation between mesodermal origin and foregut arterial supply is a classic teaching point. The spleen is thus grouped with foregut structures in blood supply tables.

explanation_incorrect.A: The spleen is mesodermal, not endodermal, and its supply is celiac via the splenic artery, not the SMA.
explanation_incorrect.B: The spleen is not midgut in origin; the SMA supplies midgut structures.
explanation_incorrect.C: The origin is correct, but the spleen has a foregut blood supply through the celiac trunk, not the SMA.
explanation_incorrect.D: The spleen is not ectodermal and is not supplied by the inferior phrenic artery.

educationalObjective: The spleen is mesodermal (from dorsal mesogastrium) yet has a foregut blood supply through the celiac trunk and splenic artery.
